title: 15th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The sitting ran from 10:30 to 11:43. Most of it was a debate on the President's decision to return the Courts Act amendment bill (reducing the Supreme Court bench from seven judges to five) to the Majlis for reconsideration. The Majority Leader moved that the bill go to committee for further amendment, opposition and some other members argued it should be dropped or that it conflicts with the Constitution, and the committee referral passed 50 to 7. The Majlis then appointed two members to the Police Board by 64 votes to none, and referred an ambassador nomination and a rules amendment to committees. The text layer is somewhat garbled, so some individual arguments are summarised loosely.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Proposed sending the returned Courts Act bill to committee, saying pending Judicial Service Commission cases make the bill's judge-reduction timeline unworkable.
Raised a point of order, saying the President's letter did not specifically state that the bill had been passed contrary to the Constitution.
Presented the Security Services Committee report on candidates for the two Police Board seats.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said the bill was unconstitutional and that cases against Supreme Court judges had already begun, so the bill's timeline no longer works.
Criticised government economic decisions and what he described as police treatment of MDP women protesters.
Argued the bill and related moves aim to bring independent institutions such as the Anti-Corruption Commission under government control.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said MDP members and many lawyers had warned in committee that the bill conflicted with the Constitution, yet it was passed quickly without enough time.
Said the Majlis loses power when it passes bills as the President directs, and asked that the bill be opened for public comment until April.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Said bills need more time and consultation rather than quick passage, and that both the courts and the Majlis should work independently.
Welcomed the President's decision to return the bill and said such bills should not be rushed in future.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Recalled the Supreme Court being locked down and judges detained under the earlier MDP government, and said the Supreme Court bench has changed with governments.
Questioned whether seven Supreme Court judges are needed for the population, citing about MVR 7.9 million a year for two more judges.
Asked why opposition parties did not reform the judiciary while in government.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Seconded the committee referral and said the Courts Act has been amended before, so this change is not unprecedented.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the Majlis should legislate more responsibly and consult lawyers, and that he did not accept parking the bill in committee; he wanted it set aside.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Noted legal advice that parts of the bill conflict with the Constitution, and said the bill should be removed from the Majlis.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said the handling of the bill showed the Majlis passing laws to suit the leader's wishes, and supported removing the bill from the Majlis.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said past MDP-led governments changed Supreme Court judges, and that the bill was discussed in the PNC parliamentary group before being passed.
Supported the motion to send the bill to committee.

decisions: The returned Courts Act (5th amendment) bill was sent to the Judiciary Committee for further amendment, 50 to 7.
Mohamed Sadiq was approved as a Police Board member from the public, 64 to 0.
Ahmed Mizmadh was approved as a Police Board member from the public, 64 to 0.
Ashraf Rasheed replaces Ibrahim Naseem on the Judiciary Committee.
The nomination of Gila Ali as non-resident ambassador to Denmark was sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
The Majlis rules amendment from Ahmed Naseer was sent to the General Committee.
The Monetary Authority Deputy Governor item was closed after the Deputy Governor resigned.
